title: Implement streaming lease coordinator and cancellation-safe shutdown for Go SDK
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add a streaming 'lease' coordinator abstraction to the Go SDK that centralizes ownership of an in-progress streaming session and enables cancellation-safe shutdown, deterministic draining, and retry-friendly reconnect semantics. This ticket addresses intermittent races where multiple goroutines attempt to close/renew a stream, causing duplicate in-flight requests, leaked goroutines, or cancelled contexts that break reconnects.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a LeaseCoordinator type in the Go SDK that can Acquire/Release a lease for a streaming session and expose a Read/Write shutdown sequence.
Streams gracefully drain buffered tokens and metrics when ctx.Err() == context.Canceled or deadline exceeded, without leaking goroutines or leaving unrecovered state.
Reconnect path: when a transient network error occurs, the SDK can attempt a bounded retry within a configurable retry window while preserving request idempotency and consumer ordering.
No new data is delivered to stream consumers after Release unless a fresh lease is acquired.
Unit and integration tests cover cancellation races, forced shutdown, reconnect with pending KV cache, and observability hooks for lease transitions.
Benchmarks demonstrate <=5% added p99 tail latency for typical 512-token sequences with lease coordination enabled.
design_decisions: LeaseCoordinator is a small sync'ed struct that holds a lease token (uuid) and a generation counter; Acquire returns the current generation and a cancel-safe handle.
Use a single ownership goroutine pattern: only the lease owner performs low-level network reads/writes; consumers interact via channels protected by the lease generation to avoid races.
When a context cancellation is observed by the owner, we transition through states: Draining -> Closed; consumers receive an explicit 'EOF-cancelled' terminal event instead of raw context errors.
Retries are bounded by a per-stream retry window and prefer reconnecting to a compatible model variant; lease remains invalidated on certain unrecoverable errors (auth, model-mismatch).
Expose a lightweight telemetry hook (OnLeaseChange) so Console can show lease state transitions on per-route dashboards.
implementation_notes: Add pkg streaming/lease.go implementing LeaseCoordinator with Acquire(ctx) (LeaseHandle, err) and LeaseHandle.Release(ctx) error.
Refactor existing stream reader/writer in client/streaming.go to delegate ownership checks to LeaseCoordinator before performing socket reads/writes.
Introduce a small state machine for stream owner: Idle -> Active -> Draining -> Terminated and document transition triggers in comments.
Implement deterministic draining: owner signals consumers with a terminal frame that includes reason (cancelled, deadline, EOF, network) and last acked token index.
Keep public API backwards compatible: Stream() method still returns a ReadCloser-like iterator; under the hood it obtains a lease and returns a wrapper that fails fast if lease lost.
Config knobs: MaxLeaseRetries (3), LeaseRetryWindow (10s), DrainingTimeout (250ms), ObserveLeaseChanges bool. Defaults set in config.go.
Add robust tests using a fake transport that can inject delays, network errors, and partial frames to exercise races.
test_plan: Unit tests for LeaseCoordinator: concurrent Acquire/Release, release under blocked consumer, generation mismatch handling.
Integration tests using test-server: simulate context cancellation during streaming, verify graceful terminal frames and no goroutine leaks (use goroutine count assertions).
Chaos test: inject intermittent TCP resets and ensure reconnects happen only within retry window and do not duplicate events to consumer.
Load benchmark: measure p50/p95/p99 for 512-token and 2048-token sequences with and without lease coordinator enabled.
Add flakiness guard: run key tests 50x in CI on linux-amd64 to validate race-free behavior.
rollout_plan: Feature gate LeaseCoordinator behind config flag streaming.lease.enabled (default true for beta). Roll out to SDK canary channel first, collect telemetry for 72 hours, then enable default for all clients in sdk-go-0.28.0. If we observe >0.5% increase in stream error rate or >10% goroutine counts increased, rollback by toggling the feature flag.
risks: Introduced coordination may add latency or contention under extreme concurrency; mitigated by owner-only IO path and small critical sections.
Edge-case: external consumers that relied on raw ctx.Err() might receive terminal events instead; document behaviour and provide migration guide.
If lease state transitions are mis-implemented, consumers may observe duplicate frames; thorough testing required.
updates: 2025-03-12 - Maya Chen: Created ticket after several incidents where ctx cancellation raced with reconnects in production. Spike confirmed goroutine leaks when multiple routines attempted to close streams concurrently.
2025-03-14 - Liam O'Connor: Proposed initial API shape for LeaseCoordinator; sketched Acquire/Release handle and generation-based read guard. Posted design doc to Confluence link above.
2025-03-17 - Engineering review: core eng team agreed on owner-only IO pattern. PM (Arjun Patel) requested telemetry hook for Console dash. Added ObserveLeaseChanges hook to design.
2025-03-19 - Implementation: started refactor of client/streaming.go; added streaming/lease.go skeleton and unit tests for Acquire/Release. Opened draft PR #412.

2025-03-22 - QA: found a race in the draining path where consumer Read could block waiting for owner after ctx cancellation; fixed by adding non-blocking terminal frame send and fallback deadline. Added integration test reproducing the race.
2025-03-25 - Performance: benchmark shows 2% p99 overhead at 512 tokens. Logged follow-up ENG-43145 to optimize channel allocations during high concurrency.
2025-03-25 - Next: finish integration tests, merge PR, and enable canary rollout in SDK canary channel.
